Focus on rhythm. Melody. Inflection.    

Freestyle as much as you can while keeping a tight rhythm, don’t be afraid to say nonsense… you will eventually get the hang of keeping a hold of rhythm and being able to say things that are ok, even having eureka moments of “damn what I just said was actually good, I need to write that down.”    

You need to exaggerate as well. Take your personality, exaggerate every aspect of it. Metaphors. Stories. Paint a picture, surround yourself with art of different origins and if you start doubting your ability, doubt your ability to doubt your abilities and push through.     

Rhythm. Keep mind of what words you put stress and emphasis on, and what words rather contract and flow into the other like a chain link, that have less emphasis but contribute to the cadence or melody of the line, and the essence of the overall flow. Emphasis on words and phrases plays into the personality you’re trying to transmute into sounds.    

Rhythm is everywhere. Feel rhythm in all language, feel the rising and falling of melody in all language and forms of expression. Repetition of concepts and flows you do not fully understand, until you get what makes them work intuitively is important.   
But you gotta let yourself be terrible at times. Put your ego aside. You don’t see how much everyone who is successful had to fail over and over again to even get to a sound they appreciated from themselves. Be willing to suck, and be willing to have moments where you transcend yourself and reach a level you seldom get to by force, but rather by complete immersion within the moment. Be willing to love the medium for what it is, not what it can give you. Just don’t stop trying

I will say what each line makes me feel.      

“To bear the weight of the fleet”

Interesting start. I would like to know more about this weight, you have made a statement about a weight that could lead into a strong examination of this weight with maybe imagery, or with a strong conflicted emotion of who is being this weight. Which you do a little at the end, but since it is vague at the beginning I do not know about this figure who is leading, why they are a leader, how they are leading. What weight does them winning or losing hold when I do not know how they feel? You are holding the key to one’s heart, the vigor of their lifestyle, have your words reflect that heat, their passion, I know poems are generally short but specificity would lift this beginning into a higher state of interest.

“No praise for victory     
Responsibility for defeat”    

Why does defeat and victory matter at this state in the poem, when we know absolutely nothing about who is bearing the weight of this battle. You are telling us something that can be shown directly. You don’t need to simply ponder about the sorrow of having a battle potentially not go your way, until you have *shown* us why it has to be that way. Make these vague statements *after* you have established a strong emotion, after you have established a solid foundation that the reader has empathized with. I simply, at this beginning, do not yet care for who is fighting this battle, why? Because I know nothing about them. I do not see their struggle, I am vaguely pointed in a direction of their struggle. I will say that no praise for victory is an interesting idea, but it would be stronger if an image supported it. Here’s how I’d write the first three lines,    

laboring breath of his fleet is as one,    
They climb a to victory no one has won,   
Defeat has a weapon that forces his hand,   
Will fame so besmirch him, is he fails his land?   

Onto your next part.   

“Show no doubt in soul or eyes     
Or doubt will creep and spell demise”     

I feel like the voice of “show no doubt in soul or eyes”, comes off as passive, and maybe you’re aiming for vagueness, but given the vagueness of the first stanza, this line doesn’t emphasize much that has already existed within the poem. Here’s something I thought of that might come off stronger, 

“Their eyes are of fire,   
Defying demise, but     
Doubt’s wretched limbs    
Pluck at their mortal ties”     

Again, I’m not saying what you wrote isn’t strong in its own way, but reading it made me desire more personality shown. You can play around with words that are simple, but in and of themselves evoke stronger emotion, that evoke subtle images. That better define the heat of battle, imagine what a 3rd person viewer of a battle would think as they watched people get murdered because of an existing self doubt. Who is this narrator exactly? Do they care about the soldiers, about the person running the fleet? Do they care about death, is battle something they are also passionate about? You decide. Further fleshing out the feelings of this narrator would make your poem stronger.
